groups.title: The Nature of God
groups.note: Indivisibility and one divine essence are theological conclusions drawn from Scripture rather than statements expressed in those exact technical terms.

groups.title: Relationships Within the Trinity
groups.note: The terms eternal generation, procession, perichoresis, and inseparable operations are theological formulations that explain the combined biblical witness.

teachings.title: God is One
teachings.detail: There is only one true God, not three Gods.

verses.label: Deuteronomy 6:4
verses.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.

verses.label: Isaiah 45:5
verses.text: I am the LORD, and there is no other; there is no God but Me. I will equip you for battle, though you have not known Me,

verses.label: 1 Corinthians 8:4
verses.text: So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.

topic.title: How can the Son and Spirit be God without there being more than one God?
topic.theme: One God: Monotheism and the Trinity
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that confessing the Son and Spirit as God introduces neither a second or third God nor a single Person under several names: Hilary, Hippolytus, Ambrose, Augustine, Novatian, Waterland and Bickersteth all reject the Sabellian or modalist reading, and Hilary, Ambrose, Augustine, Waterland, Bickersteth and Warfield read texts like 1 Corinthians 8:6 and 'I and the Father are one' as including the Son in the one God while keeping the Persons distinct.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: I shall take care that in our assertion of the One true God I give no cover to the Sabellian heresy that the Father is one Person with the Son

teachings.title: God is Spirit
teachings.detail: God is not inherently a material or bodily being.

verses.label: John 4:24
verses.text: God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”

verses.label: Luke 24:39
verses.text: Look at My hands and My feet. It is I Myself. Touch Me and see—for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.”

topic.title: Does God have a body or passions, and how is Scripture's bodily language to be read?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: All the authors who address the question agree that God has no body and that Scripture's bodily and emotional language is not to be taken literally.

quote.author: Daniel Waterland
quote.text: We, more consistently, suppose three Persons equal, in all respects; none of them singly part of God; but every one perfect God.

teachings.title: God is Eternal
teachings.detail: God has no beginning or end.

verses.label: Psalm 90:2
verses.text: Before the mountains were born or You brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting You are God.

verses.label: Revelation 1:8
verses.text: “I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, who is and was and is to come—the Almighty.

topic.title: Is God eternal and unchangeable, beyond time and increase?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that God is eternal and unchangeable: Gregory of Nyssa, Augustine, Athanasius, Novatian, Ambrose and Irenaeus each deny that the divine nature has a beginning, increase, loss, temporal succession, deliberation over the uncertain, or emptiness.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: Since, then, it belongs to the creation to have a beginning, that will be alien from the uncreated nature which belongs to the creation.

teachings.title: God is Uncreated
teachings.detail: God exists independently of creation.

verses.label: Acts 17:24–25
verses.text: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands. Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.

verses.label: John 1:3
verses.text: Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made.

topic.title: How does God's nature transcend creatures, and does He need anything from them?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that God transcends creatures and needs nothing from them, but they come at this from different angles.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: for he from whom death is not absent is not in his essence immortal. But again; if these terms signify the absence neither of death nor of destruction, either they are applied falsely to the God overall, or else they comprise within themselves some different meaning.

teachings.title: God is Immutable
teachings.detail: God’s divine nature does not change.

verses.label: Malachi 3:6
verses.text: “Because I, the LORD, do not change, you descendants of Jacob have not been destroyed.

verses.label: James 1:17
verses.text: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.

topic.title: How do God's knowledge, will and creative action work without change or succession?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: Augustine, Gregory of Nyssa and Hilary agree that God's knowledge and will involve no change, learning or succession.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: Still Further of the Difference Between the Knowledge…
quote.text: He does not know them because they are, but they are because He knows them. For He was not ignorant of what He was about to create; therefore He created because He knew; He did not know because He created.

teachings.title: God is Invisible
teachings.detail: The divine essence cannot be seen by physical eyes.

verses.label: 1 Timothy 1:17
verses.text: Now to the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.

verses.label: John 1:18
verses.text: No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known.

topic.title: How can the invisible Father be known and seen through the Son?
topic.theme: God the Father
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that the invisible Father is known only through the Son, and none thinks God can be seen by natural power or comprehended in his essence.

quote.author: Novatian
quote.place: He Proves Also that the Words Spoken to Philip Make…
quote.text: But if Christ Himself had been the Father, why did He promise as future, a reward which He had already granted and given?

teachings.title: God is Omnipresent
teachings.detail: God is not limited by physical space.

verses.label: Psalm 139:7–10
verses.text: Where can I go to escape Your Spirit? Where can I flee from Your presence? If I ascend to the heavens, You are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there. If I rise on the wings of the dawn, if I settle by the farthest sea, even there Your hand will guide me; Your right hand will hold me fast.

verses.label: Jeremiah 23:24
verses.text: “Can a man hide in secret places where I cannot see him?” declares the LORD. “Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” declares the LORD.

topic.title: Is God present everywhere without being contained in a place?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: All the authors (Hilary of Poitiers, Novatian, Gregory of Nyssa, Irenaeus of Lyons, Athanasius and Augustine) agree that God is everywhere and confined by no place, containing all things rather than being contained, though they draw different consequences from this.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: There is no space where God is not; space does not exist apart from Him. He is in heaven, in hell, beyond the seas; dwelling in all things and enveloping all.

teachings.title: God is Indivisible
teachings.detail: God’s essence is not divided into parts.

verses.label: Deuteronomy 6:4
verses.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.

verses.label: John 10:30
verses.text: I and the Father are one.”

topic.title: Is God simple, so that His attributes and names are identical with His essence?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that God is simple and without parts, change or accidents, so His attributes are not things He has apart from Himself.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: for it will not be possible, if God is essentially Father, to exclude the Son from a relationship to Him thus essential.

teachings.title: God has one divine essence
teachings.detail: The three Persons possess the same undivided divine being.

verses.label: John 10:30
verses.text: I and the Father are one.”

verses.label: Hebrews 1:3
verses.text: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

topic.title: In what does the unity of the one God consist?
topic.theme: One God: Monotheism and the Trinity
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that God's unity is not that of a single solitary Person: Waterland denies that the Godhead is monoprosopos (equating that with Sabellian singularity), Hilary reads 'Believe in God, believe also in Me' as excluding a solitary God, and Athanasius rejects the Marcellian expansion-and-contraction of the Monad as leading to Sabellianism.

quote.author: Daniel Waterland
quote.text: it is from thence we discover that God is not μονοπρόσωπος, a single Hypostasis, but that the Father has his coessential and coeternal Son and Holy Spirit always in him and with him.

teachings.title: The Father is God

verses.label: John 6:27
verses.text: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.”

verses.label: 1 Corinthians 8:6
verses.text: yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.

topic.title: What is proper to the Father, and how do believers relate to him?
topic.theme: God the Father
topic.cmp: The five authors answer different questions, so they mostly complement rather than contradict one another.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: What is Said of the Father and Son Together, and What Not.
quote.text: if nothing is spoken of the Father as such, except that which is spoken of Him in relation to the Son, that is, that He is His father, or begetter, or beginning

teachings.title: The Son is God

verses.label: John 1:1
verses.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

verses.label: John 20:28
verses.text: Thomas replied, “My Lord and my God!”

verses.label: Hebrews 1:8
verses.text: But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.

topic.title: Is the Son truly and fully God, equal with the Father?
topic.theme: The Full Deity of the Son
topic.cmp: All the authors who answer agree that the Son is truly God and not a creature or lesser deity: Irenaeus, Novatian, Athanasius, Hilary, Gregory of Nyssa, Basil, Ambrose, Augustine, Owen, Waterland and Bickersteth each affirm this, and Basil and Athanasius read the session at the right hand as equality, not lower rank.

quote.author: Irenaeus of Lyons
quote.place: Chapter XI—Proofs in continuation, extracted from St
quote.text: For that according to John relates His original, effectual, and glorious generation from the Father, thus declaring, “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.”

teachings.title: The Holy Spirit is God

verses.label: Acts 5:3–4
verses.text: Then Peter said, “Ananias, how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and withhold some of the proceeds from the land? Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? How could you conceive such a deed in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God!”

verses.label: 1 Corinthians 3:16
verses.text: Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?

verses.label: 1 Corinthians 6:19
verses.text: Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;

topic.title: Is the Holy Spirit fully God, coequal and coeternal with the Father and the Son?
topic.theme: The Holy Spirit's Deity and Personhood
topic.cmp: All the authors (Ambrose, Basil, Gregory of Nyssa, Augustine, Hilary, Novatian, Irenaeus, Athanasius, Owen, Edwards, Bickersteth, Warfield) affirm that the Holy Spirit is fully God, uncreated, coeternal and equal with the Father and the Son, and owed the same faith and worship.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: It is plain then that that, from share in which all creation is excluded, is something special and peculiar to uncreated being.

teachings.title: The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct Persons

verses.label: Matthew 3:16–17
verses.text: As soon as Jesus was baptized, He went up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens were opened, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him. And a voice from heaven said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased!”

verses.label: John 14:16–17
verses.text: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever— the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.

topic.title: Are the Father, Son and Holy Spirit really distinct Persons in one undivided substance?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that the Father, Son and Holy Spirit are really distinct and not one Person under several names, and they reject Sabellius, Noetus and Praxeas while holding one God.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: How It Was Brought About that the Greeks Speak of Three…
quote.text: there is both Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit; and that the Son is not the same with the Father, nor the Holy Spirit the same with the Father or the Son

teachings.title: The Father is not the Son

verses.label: John 17:1–5
verses.text: When Jesus had spoken these things, He lifted up His eyes to heaven and said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, that Your Son may glorify You. For You granted Him authority over all people, so that He may give eternal life to all those You have given Him. Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent. I have glorified You on earth by accomplishing the work You gave Me to do. And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.

verses.label: John 8:17–18
verses.text: Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid. I am One who testifies about Myself, and the Father, who sent Me, also testifies about Me.”

topic.title: If the Son has all that the Father has, why is he not the Father?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Augustine, Waterland, and Gregory of Nyssa all deny that the Son's full possession of what the Father is makes Him the Father or strips Him of His own existence.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: The Word of God is in All Things Equal to the Father,…
quote.text: is altogether that which the Father is, yet is not the Father, because the one is Son, the other is Father

teachings.title: The Son is not the Holy Spirit

verses.text: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever—

verses.label: John 15:26
verses.text: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father—He will testify about Me.

topic.title: Which Scripture passages show the Persons to be distinct?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Daniel Waterland and Benjamin B.

quote.author: Daniel Waterland
quote.text: it is manifest that the Father and Son are there spoken of, as of two Persons; and one as Anowvng, the other as not knowing, though only in a certain respect

teachings.title: The Holy Spirit is not the Father

verses.label: John 14:16–17, 26
verses.text: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever— the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you. But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.

topic.title: Is the Holy Spirit a distinct Person who acts by his own sovereign will?
topic.theme: The Holy Spirit's Deity and Personhood
topic.cmp: All the authors who answer agree that the Holy Spirit is a personal agent who acts freely, and nearly all rest on the same text, 1 Corinthians 12:11 ("dividing to every man severally as he will"), alongside Acts 13:2 on setting apart Barnabas and Saul.

quote.author: John Owen
quote.place: The Doctrine of the Holy Trinity Explained and Vindicated
quote.text: such things were everywhere ascribed unto him in the Scripture as uncontrollably evidence him to be an intelligent, voluntary agent. This they found so plain and evident, that they could not deny but that he was a person

teachings.title: Each Person is fully God
teachings.detail: Each Person is fully God, not one-third of God.

verses.label: Colossians 2:9
verses.text: For in Christ all the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form.

verses.label: Hebrews 1:3
verses.text: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

verses.text: Then Peter said, “Ananias, how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and withhold some of the proceeds from the land? Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? How could you conceive such a deed in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God!”

topic.title: Does distinguishing the Persons imply composition, inequality or corporeality?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Gregory of Nyssa, Augustine and Irenaeus all deny that distinguishing the Persons brings composition, inequality or corporeality into God, but each argues on different ground.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: For our statement does not hereby violate the simplicity of the Godhead, since community and specific difference are not essence, so that the conjunction of these should render the subject composite

teachings.title: The three Persons are coeternal
teachings.detail: None came into existence after another.

verses.label: John 1:1–3
verses.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was with God in the beginning. Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made.

verses.label: John 17:5
verses.text: And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.

verses.label: Hebrews 9:14
verses.text: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God!

topic.title: Is the Son eternal, or was there a time when he was not?
topic.theme: The Son's Eternity and Pre-existence
topic.cmp: All the authors (Hilary, Gregory of Nyssa, Athanasius, Augustine, Basil, Novatian, Ambrose, Irenaeus, Waterland, Owen, Bickersteth, Warfield) agree that the Son is eternal and that there was no time when he was not, and most rest this on the correlation of Father and Son (an eternal Father requires an eternal Son), on the Son's being God's Word, Wisdom, Power, Life and Truth, which God was never without, and on the radiance-and-light analogy.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: we have always maintained the birth existing out of time

teachings.title: The three Persons are coequal in deity
teachings.detail: None is inferior in divine nature.

verses.label: John 5:23
verses.text: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.

verses.label: Philippians 2:6
verses.text: Who, existing in the form of God, did not consider equality with God something to be grasped,

verses.text: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

topic.title: Is the Son inferior or subordinate to the Father?
topic.theme: The Son's Equality and Texts of Subordination
topic.cmp: All the authors deny that the Son is inferior to the Father in nature, power, glory or honour.

quote.author: Novatian
quote.place: But that God, the Son of God, Born of God the Father…
quote.text: Thus making Himself obedient to His Father in all things, although He also is God, yet He shows the one God the Father by His obedience, from whom also He drew His beginning.

teachings.title: There are exactly three divine Persons
teachings.detail: Not three manifestations of one Person.

verses.label: Matthew 28:19
verses.text: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

verses.label: 2 Corinthians 13:14
verses.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.

topic.title: Are the Son and Spirit only temporary modes or expansions of one God?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Ambrose and Athanasius agree in rejecting the view that the Son and Spirit are temporary forms or mere names of the one God, but they argue on different grounds.

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.text: whereas the distinction between the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit always abiding and unchangeable, preserves the Unity of its power.

teachings.title: The Persons mutually indwell one another
teachings.detail: This is called perichoresis.

verses.label: John 14:10–11
verses.text: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words I say to you, I do not speak on My own. Instead, it is the Father dwelling in Me, performing His works. Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me—or at least believe on account of the works themselves.

verses.label: John 17:21
verses.text: that all of them may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You. May they also be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.

topic.title: What does the mutual indwelling of the Persons mean?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Hilary of Poitiers and Basil of Caesarea agree that the Father being in the Son and the Son in the Father expresses one shared nature while the Persons stay distinct.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: to confess the Father in the Son and the Son in the Father through the unity of an indivisible nature, not confused but inseparable, not intermingled but identical, not conjoined but coexisting

teachings.title: The Father is eternally Father
teachings.detail: Fatherhood is not a temporary role.

verses.text: And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed. Father, I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am, that they may see the glory You gave Me because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.

topic.title: Has God always been Father, and is 'Father' a relative name?
topic.theme: God the Father
topic.cmp: Gregory of Nyssa, Hilary of Poitiers and Augustine all treat 'Father' as a relative name that implies the Son, but they develop the point in different directions.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: But if the First Father has no cause transcending His own state, and the subsistence of the Son is invariably implied in the title of Father, why do they try to scare us

teachings.title: The Son is eternally begotten of the Father
teachings.detail: Begotten, not created.

verses.label: John 1:14, 18
verses.text: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth. No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known.

verses.label: John 5:26
verses.text: For as the Father has life in Himself, so also He has granted the Son to have life in Himself.

topic.title: Is the Son truly the Father's natural Son, begotten rather than made or created?
topic.theme: The Eternal Generation of the Son
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that the Son is the Father's true, natural Son, begotten from His substance and neither created nor adopted.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: The creation of the world is sufficient evidence to me that Thou art wise; and I am sure that Thy Wisdom, Who is like Thee, must have been begotten from Thyself.

topic.cmp: All the authors who address the question affirm that the Spirit proceeds from or belongs to the Son as well as the Father, but they ground and qualify this differently.

quote.text: if He, too, was called a Son, He would certainly be called the Son of both, which is most absurd, since no one is son of two, save of father and mother

teachings.detail: Not by different divine natures.

topic.title: Which things are said of God substantially, and which relatively?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Augustine's distinction between absolute and relative predication, the reply to the Arian claim that every predicate names God's substance, and whether anything is said of God by accident.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: He proceeds to refute those arguments which the heretics…
quote.text: some things are also predicated of Him relatively, i.e. not in respect to Himself, but to something not Himself, as He is called Father in respect to the Son, and Lord in respect to the creature that serveth Him

teachings.title: The Father loves the Son eternally

verses.label: John 17:24

topic.title: Is the Holy Spirit properly named Love and Gift within the Trinity?
topic.theme: The Spirit's Procession, Names and Mission
topic.cmp: Augustine of Hippo is the chief advocate of naming the Holy Spirit Love and Gift: he argues that the Spirit is the consubstantial communion and mutual love of Father and Son, is specially called by what both share in common ('Spirit', 'holy', love), and is relational as Gift, so that he is not a Son because he comes forth as given rather than born.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: The Holy Spirit Also is Equal to the Father and the Son…
quote.text: Therefore the Holy Spirit, whatever it is, is something common both to the Father and Son. But that communion itself is consubstantial and co-eternal

topic.theme: Worship, Glory and Baptism in the Triune Name
topic.cmp: The authors agree that glorifying God adds nothing to him and that the Son shares the Father's glory rather than lacking it, but they come at the topic from different angles.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: He had not lost His former being, but He had become what He was not before; He had not abdicated His own position, yet He had taken ours; He prays that the nature which He had assumed may be promoted to the glory which He had never renounced.

topic.title: Do Christ's sayings of dependence mean the Son lacks his own divine power and will?
topic.theme: The Son's Equality and Texts of Subordination
